text:
ajay: heads up — noticed a spike of trivy worker failures in prod yesterday when archive-mode was enabled. lots of S3 put errors and KMS decrypt failures, then jobs requeued. attaching small log snippet below. anyone seen this pattern before?

ajay: ```
2026-03-19T22:14:03Z trivy-worker[pid=34] ERROR s3: PutObject failed: AccessDenied: Access Denied
status code: 403, request id: abc123
caused by: kms:Decrypt AccessDenied for key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111:key/xxxx
requeueing scan job 987654321
```

maria: which cluster/region? only prod?

ajay: prod eu-west-1, only the archived-scan queue (archive-mode=true). dev/staging unaffected.

liam: could be KMS key policy or the role used by the scanner pod lost decrypt permission after the RBAC tweak last week. did we change any kms policies?

tina: we rolled through an RBAC+IRSA change on Mon but that should only affect deploy-role. will check infra audit logs.

ajay: audit shows a kms:RevokeGrant event ~2026-03-18 03:02 UTC on the customer-managed key used by scanner. grant id g-7f2c. suspicious.

scanner-bot: automated: trivy-worker-archive-queue has 24 failing jobs in last 12h. avg requeues 3x. rule: scanner-orchestrator.failure-rate -> page on-call if >20 in 1h.

maria: ok quick mitigation: can we disable archive-mode for the scanner fleet until we sort KMS? reduces S3/KMS pressure.

liam: agreed. archive-mode toggles in config map config/scanner-operators: set archiving.enabled=false and restart deployment scanner-archive. I'm +1 for immediate toggle.

ajay: toggled to false at 22:25 UTC, new jobs processed normally. backlog draining now.

tina: digging into grant revoke: looks like a terraform apply removed a grant when we rolled in the role consolidation change. will open an infra PR to restore grant and add a test.

security-oncall: please open a postmortem ticket and include what CVEs were resurfacing due to the requeue noise. also we need to decide if suppression rules suppressed anything critical while scanner flapped.

ajay: quick vuln triage note — during the backlog we saw a burst of results referencing yaml-parser v1.3.2 -> CVE-2025-3210 (high) and libhttp v2.0.0 (moderate). both have patches. suspect some teams didn't get scans for a day during the flap.

maria: prioritize CVE-2025-3210 (yaml-parser) as P1 for infra and platform images. libhttp we can P2 and schedule regular patch window.

liam: proposed remediation plan:
- restore KMS grant (infra PR)
- add integration test that runs a sample archive-mode scan in CI (pre-apply)
- add a suppressions-sync healthcheck so we don't drop suppression mappings during DB locks
- after KMS restored, toggle archive-mode back and monitor for 1h

tina: infra PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/pulls/452 restores grant + adds CloudTrail alert for grant revoke. also adding IAM change approval step for KMS grants.

scanner-bot: lifecycle: infra PR 452 merged -> deploying scanner-archive v2.1.

ajay: after restore we ran 5 archive scans successfully. archive-mode re-enabled 2026-03-20T01:10Z. no further decrypt errors.

security-oncall: good. action items for follow-up:
- infra: add automated check for kms:Decrypt permission during deploys (liam/tina)
- eng-ml: run a targeted re-scan of images built between 2026-03-17 and 2026-03-19 (ajay/maria)
- product-security: notify teams with failing scans and request patching for yaml-parser CVE-2025-3210 (maria/security-oncall)
- devex: add suppression-sync healthcheck to console alerting (liam)

maria: noted. i'll create the vuln tracker tickets and tag owners.

tina: also +1 to add a short-term dashboard for archive-queue latency and KMS decrypt error rate. helps ops during incidents.

ajay: thanks all. tagging this thread for the postmortem. I'll attach the CVE list and the re-scan results once done. :thumbsup:
